in_arabic.name: ذكر
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من الفعل ذكر، ويعني تذكير الله تعالى وتذكر الأحداث والمواقف المهمة في حياة المسلم، وهو من الأسماء التي تعبر عن الإيمان والتوحيد.

in_urdu.name: ذکر
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی یاد، اہم واقعات کی یاد
in_urdu.long_meaning: ذکر نام اللہ کی یاد اور اہم واقعات کی یاد سے ماخوذ ہے، جو مسلم کی زندگی میں اہم کردار ادا کرتا ہے، اور یہ نام ایمان اور توحید کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ذكر
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की याद, महत्वपूर्ण घटनाओं की याद
in_hindi.long_meaning: ذكر नाम भगवान की याद और महत्वपूर्ण घटनाओं की याद से लिया गया है, जो मुस्लिम जीवन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है, और यह नाम विश्वास और एकेश्वरवाद का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: ذکر
in_pashto.meaning: د الله یاد، مهمو پیښو یاد
in_pashto.long_meaning: ذکر نوم د الله یاد او مهمو پیښو یاد څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د مسلمان په ژوند کې مهم رول لوبوي، او دا نوم د ایمان او توحید نښه ده.

in_english.name: Zikr
in_english.meaning: Remembrance of God, remembering important events
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zikr originates from the Arabic root 'ذ-ك-ر' (ذَكَرَ), meaning to remember or remind. In Islamic context, Zikr refers to the remembrance of God, recitation of Quranic verses, and reflection on significant events. It signifies a person's commitment to faith, spiritual growth, and mindfulness.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic tradition, Zikr (also known as Dhikr or Tasawwuf) refers to the practice of continuous remembrance and glorification of Allah through various methods such as recitation of Dhikr phrases, chanting, meditation, and verbal or silent supplications. This practice has been an integral part of Islamic culture and has been widely practiced by Muslims for centuries. Zikr sessions are commonly held in mosques, shrines, or private homes, and many Islamic communities and Sufi orders have been devoted to this practice. It is a communal activity as well as a personal one, causing a sense of unity and togetherness among believers.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Zikr is a means of drawing closer to Allah and strengthening one's faith. By focusing on the remembrance of Allah, Muslims are able to purify their thoughts and emotions, overcome distractions, and develop a deeper connection with their Creator. Zikr is also believed to bring about inner peace, tranquility, and a sense of purpose in life. Through the practice of Zikr, Muslims seek to purify their hearts, overcome their passions and weaknesses, and attain nearness to Allah. Ultimately, the purpose of Zikr is to please Allah and seek His mercy and forgiveness.
